pool.text: Islamic forces captured Kalapa, later named Jayakarta under Banten Sultanate.
VOC seized Jayakarta and rebuilt it as the trading port Batavia.
VOC response to Chinese labour unrest led to a massacre of Chinese residents.
VOC designated a Chinese quarter at Diestpoort, later known as Glodok.
Indonesian independence was proclaimed in Jakarta on 17 August.
Jakarta reinstated as the capital of the unitary Republic of Indonesia.
Jakarta acquired the status of a Special Capital Region (DKI).
Legislation formally reaffirmed Jakarta as Indonesia's Special Capital Region.
The national legislative complex began as the CONEFO project.
Governor Ali Sadikin launched the Kampung Improvement Program for dense kampungs.
Asian financial crisis sparked student protests and widespread violence in Jakarta.
President Suharto resigned amid mounting political pressure.
Thousand Islands elevated to an administrative regency for better public services.
Jakarta residents directly elected the governor for the first time.
Governor Joko Widodo introduced the Healthy Jakarta Card programme.
KJS merged into the national JKN health insurance system.
Air pollution estimated to cause over 10,000 premature deaths annually.
Universal health coverage reached 98.5% of Jakarta's population.
Special‑region law defines Jakarta as national economic centre after capital transfer.
Jakarta's GRDP reached Rp 3,679.36 trillion with 4.90% growth.
